audit.whatIsWrong: All seven rows were wrong. The chart read Swain, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Swain while the whys say the exact opposite story: Level 1 even, Swain owns 2 through 5, you flip at 6, Swain takes first item, you take two items.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Skill, Swain, Swain, Swain, Volibear, Swain, Volibear — an exact match for the whys and for the 55.31% win rate, which comes from surviving to the item game rather than winning lane.
audit.corrected: All seven rows set to packet, paired across both layers, with ratings inverted to match.

audit.why: Spike order is right and unusually specific already: Swain's 3-5 poke window, your level 6 Stormbringer flip, his first-item Rylai's restoration, your two-item scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove was written as a bolt to dodge on the way in, and Demonic Ascension as a drain to simply avoid. Neither statement carries the mechanic that decides the fight.
audit.why: Nevermove roots on its RETURN trip, not the outbound — the bolt passing you once is the cue to step in, and Swain can then pull the rooted target. It is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s. Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s and persists indefinitely only while he is draining a champion, so disengaging ends the form early rather than waiting it out. Ravenous Flock heals him off Soul Fragments and permanently raises his max health, which is the actual reason for the anti-heal buy.
audit.corrected: Return-trip root, 120s R with the walk-away cue, and Grievous Wounds tied to Ravenous Flock.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] credits Death's Hand with a slow.
audit.why: Death's Hand is piercing bolts with no slow. Vision of Empire (22s at rank 1) is the ability that slows and reveals.
audit.corrected: Slow attributed to Vision of Empire.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Don’t fight into it. Track it before every engage. - Swain Nevermove: A returning bolt that roots enemies it hits — his catch tool. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Swain Demonic Ascension: 120s, and the form only lasts while he is draining a champion — walk out and it ends early. - Swain Nevermove: 12s at rank 1, and it roots on the return trip, never the outbound one.

edits.before: His drain. Don’t fight into it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: R is 120s and ends the moment nobody is left in drain range.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Ravenous Flock heals off Soul Fragments — buy Grievous Wounds early.

edits.before: Charging Q into a waiting Demonic Ascension — losing the stun before you land it means you took the whole trade for nothing and your W mark expires un-cashed.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the return trip, not the outbound one — step in right after the bolt first passes you, not while it is still travelling out.

edits.before: Kite your Q window with Q slow and R sustain
edits.after: Slow you with Vision of Empire, then drain

notes: Every one of the seven chart rows disagreed with its own why here — the page told the player Swain wins levels 2-5 in prose while the chart showed those stages as even. packet.levelChart and the whys agree exactly, so the fix was unambiguous.
